title: Quarterly flight deck and initiative gateway for cross-functional commitments
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: As Redwood scales, teams are repeatedly surface-blocked by unclear cross-functional dependencies during quarterly planning. The current approach (email + one-off spreadsheets + ad-hoc meetings) creates rework and shifting priorities when enterprise initiatives (Dedicated/Private launches, runtime releases) intersect with product roadmaps.

This ticket scopes a lightweight 'Quarterly Flight Deck' and an 'Initiative Gateway' process to be run at the start of each quarter to: 1) consolidate company-level OKRs into an executable set of initiatives; 2) provide a dependency-catalog and gating checklist for teams to commit; 3) produce a single canonical artifact (flight deck) that engineering, security, and GTM teams use for capacity/cost decisions.

Why now: Q1 launch cadence includes multiple Dedicated capacity features and a Private deployment compliance push. We need a repeatable playbook to reduce last-minute scope cuts and to align capacity commitments with reserved budget and engineering cycles.
scope_included:
- Facilitate a 3-hour cross-functional planning workshop (PM/ENG/Design/SRE/Sales+CS).
- Produce an editable flight deck template with OKR-to-initiative mapping and explicit dependency lanes.
- Create an Initiative Gateway checklist (security, infra cost estimate, rollout plan, rollback criteria).
- Publish a dependency catalog for each initiative with owner and delivery window.
- Integrate outputs into roadmap hub and set initial rollout gates.
scope_excluded:
- Full automation of gating in the console (out of scope for Q1).
- Rewriting company OKR definitions (we will consume existing OKRs).
- Deep resourcing negotiations with sales/finance (we will surface gaps but not resolve them in-scope).
success_metrics:
- Reduce number of mid-quarter scope decommits by 50% vs last cycle.
- >80% of initiatives have a named dependency owner and estimated completion window in the flight deck.
- Leadership (PM/ENG/OPS) signs off on the flight deck for at least 90% of company initiatives before sprint planning.
- Post-mortem severity incidents attributable to misaligned cross-team dependencies reduced by 30% in the quarter.

stakeholders: Engineering: Daniel Park (assignee), lead ENG owners for runtime and dedicated teams
acceptance_criteria:
- Flight deck template available and editable in Confluence.
- Intake form collects initiative name, OKR mapping, primary owner, dependencies, estimated engineering effort, security checklist status, and target release window.
- At least 12 business-critical initiatives have completed intake and are reviewed in the workshop.
- Leadership signoff recorded as a comment on the Confluence page.
- Roadmap hub populated with initiative IDs and dependency links for program-level visibility.
operational_risks:
- Risk: Owners under-estimate engineering effort causing downstream slippage. Mitigation: Require an initial engineering estimate with RAG risk flag and host two follow-up deep-dive sessions before signoff.
- Risk: Security signoff may lag for Private deployment initiatives. Mitigation: Pre-identify high-risk initiatives and schedule a dedicated security pre-review one week before the workshop.
- Risk: Workshop attendance gaps. Mitigation: Run two workshop slots and record a condensed playback with required sign-off action items.
communication_plan:
- Pre-work: Distribute intake form and template to team leads 7 days before workshop.
- During: Live notes and action items tracked in the Confluence flight deck.
- Post-workshop: Publish final flight deck and a 1-page summary to #company-roadmap slack channel and tag stakeholders.
- Follow-up: Weekly 30-minute drop-in for 3 weeks to triage outstanding dependencies.
